source_title: Maserati Grecale Folgore facelift - Autocar India
source_excerpt:
The Maserati Grecale Folgore is Maserati's first all-electric SUV, sold as a single variant with a 105kWh battery (97kWh usable) and one electric motor on each axle for all-wheel drive. Together the motors make 550hp and 820Nm, which is enough for 0-100kph in 4.1 seconds and a top speed of 220kph.
The facelifted model launched in India on October 30, 2026, at a starting price of Rs 1.90 crore, as part of the 2027 Grecale Folgore line-up. It brings a claimed range of up to 580km, a shark-nose front bumper inspired by the MCPura supercar, new wheel designs and a refreshed cabin, and it takes on the Porsche Macan EV.
105kWh battery (97kWh net) on a 400V platform; two permanent-magnet motors, one per axle
Claimed range of up to 580km, up from 501km before the facelift
12.3-inch driver's display, 12.3-inch central touchscreen and 8.8-inch lower touchscreen for climate control
1,285W Sonus Faber audio with 21 speakers on offer
GT, Off-Road, Sport and Corsa drive modes, plus a Max Range mode on the Folgore
Panoramic sunroof, heated leather steering wheel and front and rear parking sensors as options
New octagonal steering wheel in perforated leather or Alcantara, a digital clock with a mineral-crystal dial and metal bezel, and metal PRND buttons with backlighting and haptic feedback
Redesigned shark-nose bumper and grille with air curtains
New 20-inch Asteria and 21-inch Crono wheels
These points are based on the launch details and Autocar India's coverage of the Grecale Folgore, and will be updated after a full road test.
The dual-motor setup delivers 550hp and 820Nm, with a claimed 0-100kph time of 4.1 seconds, which is quick for a luxury electric SUV.
The claimed range has grown to up to 580km, thanks to aerodynamic refinements, new energy management software and more efficient tyres. A dedicated Max Range mode helps stretch it further.
The shark-nose bumper, air curtains along the wheel arches and active grille shutters give the SUV a sharper look while improving airflow.
The cabin pairs three screens with a new octagonal steering wheel, a digital clock and metal drive-selector buttons with haptic backlighting.
Personalisation is a strength, with 24 exterior colours, 16 interior upholstery options and the Fuoriserie programme.
Air suspension and a 21-speaker Sonus Faber system, available on request, add to the luxury feel.
The claimed 580km range is still below the 591-641km that the Porsche Macan EV claims.
The price sits well above the Macan EV, which Autocar India lists at Rs 1.22-1.75 crore.
It charges at up to 150kW DC on a 400V platform, while Maserati's 800V GranTurismo Folgore charges at up to 270kW.
Items such as the panoramic sunroof, Sonus Faber audio, heated steering wheel and parking sensors are options, so the final price can climb above the starting figure.
There is only one variant and one powertrain to choose from.
As per our assessment, the Grecale Folgore is best suited to buyers who want a distinctive electric luxury SUV with strong performance and plenty of personalisation.
It is the brand's first all-electric SUV, with Maserati's design and Italian character.
550hp, 820Nm and a claimed 0-100kph in 4.1 seconds make it quick off the line.
A claimed range of up to 580km and a Max Range mode suit long-distance use.
24 exterior colours, 16 interior upholstery choices and the Fuoriserie programme let you tailor the car.
Air suspension, three screens and an available Sonus Faber audio system make daily use comfortable.
The buyer the Grecale Folgore suits least is the one who wants the quickest charging or the longest range in the class, as the Macan EV claims more range and the Grecale Folgore tops out at 150kW DC charging. Those who want every option fitted should also plan for a final price above the starting figure.

Maserati Grecale Folgore price & variants
Maserati Grecale Folgore price in India starts at 1.90 crore, ex-showroom, while the on-road price in Delhi is 2.02 crore. The Grecale Folgore is offered in 1 variant with a single electric powertrain.
The launch price is marginally higher than the pre-facelift Folgore, which was priced at Rs 1.89 crore (ex-showroom, before options).
Within the 2027 Grecale line-up, it sits above the Modena V6 at Rs 1.39 crore and below the 530hp Trofeo V6 at Rs 2 crore. The Folgore has 20hp more than the Trofeo, but the Trofeo is quicker to 100kph at 3.8 seconds and tops out at 285kph.
With a single variant, the main choices are the 20-inch or 21-inch wheels, the paint and interior colours, and options such as the panoramic sunroof and Sonus Faber audio.
The 21-inch wheels gain up to 53km of range with the update, while the 20-inch wheels gain up to 9km.
The Porsche Macan EV is the main rival, and Autocar India lists it at Rs 1.22-1.75 crore.
EMIs for the Grecale Folgore start at 2,92,982 a month.
Maserati Grecale Folgore has a claimed range of up to 580km, up from 501km before the facelift. Maserati credits aerodynamic changes, a new control strategy with updated energy management algorithms and more efficient tyres, and says the gain is up to 9km on 20-inch wheels and up to 53km on 21-inch wheels. The Folgore also gets active grille shutters and a Max Range mode to help it go further.
The 105kWh battery (97kWh usable) supports AC charging at up to 22kW and DC fast charging at up to 150kW. Real-world range will be lower than the claimed figure and depends on speed, wheel size, temperature and driving mode.

The new octagonal steering wheel and the new digital clock with a metal bezel
The new metal PRND drive-selector buttons with integrated backlighting
